title: History Center lights up for a monthlong Season of Lights starting Dec. 2
summary: The Chester County History Center fills its galleries with illuminated displays and decorated trees from Dec. 2 through Jan. 2, open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1. The exhibit is included with regular admission: $10 adults, $7 seniors, $5 children and students.
loc: Chester County History Center, 225 N. High St., West Chester

title: Veterans Day Parade steps off downtown Sunday, Nov. 8
summary: The borough's annual parade honoring area veterans starts at 2 p.m. and follows Gay, Church and High streets through the downtown. It is free to watch.
loc: Gay, Church and High streets, West Chester

title: Fall community clean-up meets at Rustin Park on Sunday, Nov. 8
summary: Residents, local groups and West Chester University students gather at the shed in Rustin Park at 10 a.m. for a borough-wide tidy-up, and the borough says all hands are welcome. Registration is through the link on the borough's news page.

title: Tree Commission launches a self-guided Tree Trail through the borough
summary: The West Chester Tree Trail is a walking tour of 11 notable trees or tree groups chosen to show off the borough's canopy, its history and its variety, timed for fall color. The tour takes an hour or two; pamphlets are at Borough Hall or on the borough website.
loc: Borough Hall, 401 E. Gay St., West Chester

title: Christmas Tree Train returns to the West Chester Railroad on three Sundays
summary: The two-hour excursion leaves Market Street Station at 8 a.m. on Nov. 29, Dec. 6 and Dec. 13 for Wiggins Tree Farm, where riders cut their own tree and crews load it on a flatcar for the trip back. Hot chocolate and donuts are sold on board.

title: Borough seeks volunteers for seven boards, applications due Dec. 4
summary: Borough Council is taking resumes for seats on the rail service committee, Historical Commission, Human Relations Commission, Library Board, Recreation Commission, Transportation Advisory Committee and Tree Commission. Applicants email a resume to the borough by Dec. 4 and will be scheduled for interviews.
loc: Borough Hall, 401 E. Gay St., West Chester

title: Clover Market brings 125 vendors to Westtown School Nov. 21-22
summary: The fourth annual Clover Market Holiday Market fills Westtown School's Athletic Center with makers and vintage sellers from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. both days. Admission and parking are free, with food trucks outside.

title: Victorian carolers will stroll downtown on holiday weekends
summary: Downtown West Chester's costumed Borough Balladeer Carolers return for eight free Friday and Saturday performances from Nov. 27 through Dec. 19, roaming the shopping district rather than singing at one spot.

title: WCU student and East grad delivers the Frederick Douglass lecture
summary: Aiden Tilery, a West Chester East graduate, gave the seventh annual Dr. Clifford E. DeBaptiste Frederick Douglass lecture at the university's Philips Autograph Library to about 100 people. He drew a line from Douglass to his great-grandfather, the former borough mayor, now 102, on education as the path to freedom.
loc: Philips Autograph Library, West Chester University

title: WCU marks 100 years of jazz with a three-day celebration Nov. 6-8
summary: The university honors its Criterions Jazz Ensemble, rooted in the 1920s, with a free welcome concert Friday at 7:30 p.m. in Asplundh Hall, a free masterclass with vibraphonist Stefon Harris Saturday at 2 p.m., a $100 dinner-dance Saturday night and a ticketed anniversary concert Sunday at 3 p.m. New pieces by Bob Mintzer and Orrin Evans premiere, and the WCU Foundation is raising money for a permanent jazz endowment.
loc: Asplundh Concert Hall, West Chester University
